lesson.picture: A lift door. Every time someone presses the button, the countdown restarts. The door only closes after nobody has pressed for 2 seconds. Debounce = 'do it once things go quiet'.
lesson.concept:
Debounce delays a function until calls stop for N ms. Each new call cancels the pending one. Used for search-as-you-type, resize handlers, autosave.

What interviewers check: you keep the timer in a closure (not global), you forward arguments and `this`, you clear the previous timer, and you can explain throttle as the opposite (run at most once per N ms, don't cancel).
lesson.bn: Debounce = কল আসা থেমে যাওয়ার N ms পরে একবার চালাও; প্রতিটা নতুন কল আগেরটা বাতিল করে। Timer closure-এ রাখো, args আর this forward করো। Throttle উল্টো — প্রতি N ms-এ সর্বোচ্চ একবার চালায়, বাতিল করে না।

practice.task: Add a cancel() and flush() method to debounce. flush runs the pending call immediately.
In React, why does const search = debounce(fn, 300) inside a component body not work, and what's the fix?
practice.solution:
```js
Each render creates a new debounced function with a fresh timer, so previous timers are never cleared — no debouncing. Fix: useMemo(() => debounce(fn, 300), []) or useRef to keep one instance, and cancel it in a cleanup effect.
```

cards.q: Debounce vs throttle in one line each
cards.a: Debounce: run once after calls stop for N ms (cancels pending). Throttle: run at most once per N ms (ignores extras).

cards.q: Where does the timer variable live in a debounce and why?
cards.a: In the closure of the returned function — each debounced function gets its own timer; a global would be shared and buggy.

cards.q: Why fn.apply(this, args) instead of fn()?
cards.a: To forward the original arguments and this (e.g. the event and the element) to the wrapped function.

cards.q: Give two real uses of debounce and one of throttle
cards.a: Debounce: search-as-you-type, autosave. Throttle: scroll position tracking / infinite-scroll checks.
